article.articleHeadline: Monkeypox: confusion over tests, a third would be a false positive.
article.articleSummary: One-third of PCR tests for monkeypox (Mpox) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo may be false positives, according to an international study led by the University of Geneva and published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. Analyzing over 2,700 samples from four cities, researchers found positives split into two groups: a majority with high viral load confirming infection, and about 35% with only trace viral DNA, likely due to environmental contamination. Investigations at two treatment centers detected Mpox DNA on surfaces, suggesting sample carryover. Blood analyses showed lack of antibodies in 89% of individuals flagged as falsely positive, while their rashes could be due to measles or varicella, the researchers note. False positives led to unnecessary hospitalisation or isolation and could distort epidemiological monitoring and vaccination planning. Authors recommend confirming positives with higher viral load thresholds and improving laboratory training to recognize anomalous test patterns.

triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国のMpox PCR検査における偽陽性率に関する研究報告であり、新規感染事例の発生を示すものではないが、サーベイランス精度への影響があるため継続的な注視が必要。
triage.notes: 本記事はジュネーブ大学主導の研究（The Lancet Infectious Diseases掲載）に基づくもので、DRCにおける既存のMpoxアウトブレイクの検査精度・サーベイランス体制の課題を指摘する内容。新規発生イベントではなく、既存流行への対応改善に関する続報として注視すべき。スイスは研究実施拠点であり発生国ではないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: Angola reports 19 more Mpox cases in the last 24 hours.
article.articleSummary: Angola reports 19 new mpox (monkeypox) cases in the last 24 hours, raising the total to 615 with 107 active. New infections are in Moxico East (5), Luanda (5), Cabinda (3), Moxico (2), Huambo (1), Icolo and Bengo (1), Namibe (1), and Uíge (1). Four recoveries (three in Moxico East, one in Cabinda). The Ministry of Health has reactivated the National Contingency Plan (initiated July) to detect suspected cases, confirm infections, identify contacts, and monitor spread amid border concerns with the DRC. Mpox is caused by a monkeypox virus; incubation 5–21 days; symptoms include fever, headache, fatigue, muscle pain, lymphadenopathy, and generalized skin rash. Preventive measures: hand hygiene, avoid hunting/eating primates or rodents, avoid contact with symptomatic people and contaminated materials, and protective handling of animals. The clade 1b lineage was detected in DRC in September 2023; WHO has declared mpox a global emergency; transmission is via close contact.

triage.headline_ja: アンゴラ、過去24時間でMpox新規19例を報告
triage.triage_reason: アンゴラでMpox（クレードⅠｂを含む）の症例が拡大を続けており、WHO国際緊急事態下でDRC国境地域への波及懸念もあることからIHR基準複数該当・フルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 発生国はアンゴラであり、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空。DRCは国境監視の文脈およびクレード1b起源として言及されているのみで、実際の症例発生地ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: DRC: Deaf people made aware of the risks associated with Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) centered in Ituri Province, with Kisangani highlighted as a current intervention site. Government figures report 7,541 confirmed cases and 3,639 deaths, with 1,823 recoveries. The outbreak is described as the deadliest of the DRC’s 17 Ebola episodes; the WHO warns it could exceed the 2014–2016 West Africa toll of over 11,000 deaths. In Kisangani, teams conducted a deaf-awareness session, using sign-language interpreter Gilbert Kazingufu to help participants recognize Ebola symptoms and avoid under-diagnosis due to communication barriers. No laboratory-confirmation details or infection-source data are provided in the article. The emphasis remains on public awareness and early symptom identification to curb transmission and improve care for vulnerable groups.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：エボラ出血熱のリスクについて聴覚障害者に啓発活動
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行は確認症例7,541人、死亡3,639人に達し、同国史上最悪の流行とされ、WHOが2014-2016年西アフリカ流行（死者11,000人超）を超える可能性を警告しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大事案。
triage.notes: 記事はイトゥリ州を中心とした大規模エボラ流行の継続を報じており、キサンガニでの聴覚障害者向け啓発活動が主題だが、背景となる流行そのものが極めて深刻（DRC史上最悪の17回目のエボラ流行）。ラボ確認詳細や感染源情報は記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: North Kivu: In Beni, Ebola response contractors on strike for two days are demanding four months of back pay.
article.articleSummary: Ebola response contractors in Beni, the provisional capital of North Kivu, launched a two-day strike starting September 21, 2026, over unpaid allowances. The workers—communications, community engagement, psychosocial teams, and community relays—demand three to four months of back pay that they say remains unsettled. They gathered outside the Beni Health Zone office, posted banners, erected barricades, and lit a fire at the entrance to the coordination office; police extinguished the blaze, but the strike halted work. They call on response authorities to resolve salary arrears and accuse the authorities of failing to disburse funds despite government claims. In Bunia, Ituri, in July, Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba said delays were not due to funds shortfalls, citing an “Ebola Business” controversy and pledging harmonization of primes for clinicians, community workers, and relays, with a budget extension anticipated in the revised finance law.

triage.headline_ja: 北キブ州ベニ：エボラ対応の請負業者が2日間のストライキ、4か月分の未払い賃金を要求
triage.triage_reason: エボラ対応活動における労働争議・資金未払い問題を報じるもので、新規感染拡大や症例増加を示す直接的情報はないが、対応体制の機能低下により今後の流行制御に影響を及ぼす可能性があるため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC北キブ州ベニにおけるエボラ対応要員の未払い賃金を巡るストライキが主題。エボラ症例自体の新規発生・拡大に関する具体的情報はないが、対応活動の中断は既存流行の管理能力に影響しうるため、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox in Kasaï: Nine health zones affected, and official counts that do not match.
article.articleSummary: Monkeypox outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Kasaï province affects nine health zones with 77 suspected, 16 confirmed cases and 3 deaths (Sept 20, 2026). Luebo remains the epicenter with 38 suspected, 13 confirmed and 3 deaths; Mushenge 13/3; Kanzala 11; Mikope 6; Kalonda Ouest 3; Kamuesha 2; Kitangwa 2; Ndjoko-Punda 1; Tshikapa 1. On Sept 17, the provincial government named five zones (Mushenge, Kanzala, Dekese, Luebo, Ilebo) as affected, while a separate briefing lists nine zones; Dekese and Ilebo are absent from the provincial tally, overlapping with only three names. The Sept 10 count for Luebo showed 74 cases and 8 deaths; the discrepancy with Sept 20 totals is unexplained. Lab confirmation is pending; samples have been sent to INRB. Response includes medicine shipments, rapid-response teams from Sept 10, expanded surveillance, and vaccination considerations; cholera and suspected yellow fever co-circulation reported (11 suspected).

triage.headline_ja: カサイ州のエムポックス：9つの保健地区で発生、公式集計に不一致
triage.triage_reason: DRCカサイ州で複数保健地区にまたがるエムポックス流行が拡大し死亡例も報告されており、コレラ・黄熱の共流行疑いや公式データの不一致もあることから、国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生への深刻な影響が認められる。
triage.notes: 発生地域にケニア(Busia)が含まれるが記事サマリー上はDRCカサイ州のみが主題であるため除外。公式集計の不一致（9地区 vs 5地区、9/10と9/20の症例数矛盾）は情報の信頼性に懸念があり、続報確認が必要。コレラ・黄熱の共流行疑いも要注視。

article.articleHeadline: Africa-Europe research consortium targets evidence gap keeping young children out of parasite control programs
article.articleSummary: IVM-KIDS aims to close a safety-evidence gap for ivermectin use in children under 15 kg (roughly under five years) across Africa and Europe. The four-year project (Sept 2025–Aug 2029) involves Ghana (Accra meetings), Kenya, Tanzania, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with partners LSHTM (UK), KNUST/KCCR (Ghana), KEMRI (Kenya), INRB (DRC), Liconsa and Mundo Sano (Spain), DNDi, and Swiss TPH. It will generate clinical, pharmacokinetic, safety, and regulatory data to determine whether ivermectin can be safely and effectively extended to children 5–15 kg, for use against onchocerciasis, lymphatic filariasis, scabies, and soil-transmitted helminths (including Trichuris trichiura). A new 3 mg orodispersible pediatric formulation will be evaluated alongside generic ivermectin. Existing data (2021 review of >1,000 children) showed no serious adverse events, but larger trials are needed to inform policy and potentially reach >250 million children globally in endemic regions.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ・欧州の研究コンソーシアムが、幼児を寄生虫対策プログラムから除外している証拠不足の解消を目指す
triage.triage_reason: これは新規の疾病発生報告ではなく、既存の駆虫薬（イベルメクチン）の小児向け安全性エビデンスを構築する研究プロジェクトの発表であり、公衆衛生上の急性イベントではない。

article.articleHeadline: Top News of the Day | Wednesday: UN General Assembly, Ukraine, Right to Development, Pediatric Cancer, Ebola.
article.articleSummary: At the UN General Assembly, the Security Council discussed Ukraine, with UN Deputy Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo reporting that the eight months of 2026 have seen more civilian casualties and injuries in Ukraine than all of 2025, as long-range missiles and drones strike towns far from the front lines and a 'new, dangerous' phase of full-scale invasion is underway, prompting calls to intensify peace efforts. In advance of the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Declaration on the Right to Development, world leaders urged action on equitable development amid digital and AI challenges. The WHO released pediatric cancer data across 194 countries: about 400,000 cases annually in those under 20, with survival 80-90% in high-income countries but ~40% in lower-income settings, notably for ages 15-19. In the DRC Ebola outbreak, after ~130 days, cases declined ~26% in Ituri and Upper Uele but rose 73% in North Kivu, requiring ongoing surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: 本日のトップニュース｜水曜日：国連総会、ウクライナ、開発の権利、小児がん、エボラ出血熱
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行は既知の継続事案だが、北キブ州で症例が73%増加しており、感染拡大の兆候として経過観察が必要。ただし本記事はUN総会関連ニュースの一部として簡潔に触れられているのみで、社会的関心の高まりは確認できない。
triage.notes: 記事はUN総会に関する日次ニュース概要であり、エボラに関する情報は既存流行の進捗報告（130日経過、イトゥリ・オートウエレで26%減少、北キブで73%増加）に限定される。ウクライナは疾病関連地域ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Scientists to test England's sewers for Ebola
article.articleSummary: England's sewers will be monitored for Ebola under UKHSA's Prism wastewater surveillance, expanding to detect Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, Marburg virus and Lassa fever. The scheme will sample hospital sewage and waste from busy locations, testing for multiple pathogens and early signals of outbreaks such as Covid-19 or norovirus. Ebola is not present in the UK, but the system aims to spot it early; Africa's Democratic Republic of Congo is currently experiencing a major outbreak with more than 3,000 deaths. The programme, already used to track norovirus strains, will extend to monitor variants and drug-resistant bacteria and fungi, including Klebsiella pneumoniae and Candida auris. Prism—Pathogen Risk Intelligence through Surveillance and Modelling—will run for two more years and complements existing polio wastewater surveillance, which detected polio in London in 2022 and has detected imported cases in Leeds, West Sussex, Shoreham and Sheffield.

triage.headline_ja: 英国、下水からエボラウイルスを検出する検査を実施へ
triage.triage_reason: 記事はUKの下水監視拡大が主題だが、コンゴ民主共和国（DRC）で3,000人超の死者を伴う大規模エボラ流行が現在進行中であることが明記されており、深刻性・異常性の観点でIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事本体はUKの下水サーベイランス（Prism）拡大に関する内容だが、その背景としてDRCで3,000人以上の死者を出す大規模エボラ流行が現在進行中であることが述べられている。英国（UK）は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。DRCのアウトブレイクについての詳細情報（発生数の推移、地域等）は本記事には含まれておらず、既存のRRA評価の有無を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in South Ubangi: after a second confirmed case in Bulu, Dr Mbungani calls for a response commensurate with the threat
article.articleSummary: Two Ebola cases confirmed in Bulu health zone, South Ubangi Province, signaling active community transmission. The second case tested positive at INRB and is a contact of the first fatal case in Gwaka; the patient had refused post-exposure prophylaxis and is being treated with Remdesivir. The first death occurred on September 8, 2026 in Gwaka after travel through Rwanda, Burundi, Bunia, Kisangani, Bumba, Lisala and Akula, with deterioration at Akula before admission to Gwaka General Referral Hospital. A prior June suspected case from Beni, also passing through Akula, died in Gwaka. So far, all Sud-Ubangi samples tested: two positives; others pending. Dr Mbungani calls for declaring Bulu an active outbreak, strengthening surveillance along Akula-Gwaka-Zongo, and integrating Sud-Ubangi into Fleuve Congo sans Ebola; ensure funding, isolate contacts, secure river ports, protect frontline workers with risk allowances, and engage communities.

triage.headline_ja: 南ウバンギ州でエボラ出血熱：ブル地区で2例目確認、ムブンガニ医師が脅威に見合う対応を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国南ウバンギ州で確認されたエボラ出血熱の2例目が地域内感染を示唆しており、既に死亡例も発生。複数都市を経由した移動歴があり国際的拡大リスクも懸念されるため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 患者はルワンダ・ブルンジ・ブニア・キサンガニ・ブンバ・リサラ・アクラを経由して移動しており、これらは通過地であり発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めていない。ベナン（Zongo等）も記事本文では発生地としての言及がなく除外。感染管理・資金確保・住民との協働などの必要性が医師から強調されており、社会的・行政的関心も高いと判断。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox surges in SA and 11 African countries - Juta MedicalBrief
article.articleSummary: Mpox surges in South Africa with 18 laboratory-confirmed cases, mainly in Cape Town (15), plus 3 in Gauteng and 1 in KwaZulu-Natal. Ages 23–50 (median 36.5); 18 men and 1 woman. Thirteen cases occurred between 13 August and 17 September, signaling rapid local transmission; one case had traveled to Spain. Limited Tecovirimat vaccine doses have been secured for outbreak response. Across Africa, 11 countries report 1,153 cases and seven deaths in six weeks (6 July–16 August), with Madagascar accounting for 785 cases—the highest; Angola 184; Kenya 94; DRC 41; Cameroon 28. Since January 2025, mpox has affected 35 African countries; regional totals reach 52,424 cases and 238 deaths (through 16 August 2026). Globally, 65,784 cases and 264 deaths across 105 countries (through 31 July 2026). The WHO extends mpox recommendations to August 2027; Africa CDC had ended PHECS in January 2026, vaccination central to ongoing control.

triage.headline_ja: 南アフリカとアフリカ11か国でエムポックスが急増 - Juta MedicalBrief
triage.triage_reason: 南アフリカでの急速な人-人感染拡大とアフリカ35か国・5万人超の症例、死亡例の継続的発生が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ngoma Festival in Kisangani: the public subjected to handwashing to prevent Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Public health measures at the 16th Ngoma Festival in Kisangani, Tshopo Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, on 23 September 2026 require attendees to wash hands at buckets at the entrance of the main venue to prevent Ebola virus disease (EVD). The initiative responds to Ebola activity in Kisangani and the wider Tshopo area and is welcomed by festival-goers such as Jean-Pierre Alongo and Divine Lotsima, who say it enhances safety. The festival, themed 'Art at the Heart of Communities', features slam, dance, theater and storytelling with participants from Kisangani and visitors from Kinshasa, Matadi and Congo Brazzaville; Burundian artists did not attend this edition. The article notes ongoing Ebola circulation in the city but provides no lab-confirmation details or case counts.

triage.headline_ja: キサンガニのンゴマ祭り：エボラ対策として来場者に手洗いを義務化
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国キサンガニ周辺でエボラウイルス病の継続的な発生が言及されており、大規模な祭りイベントでの人的接触も伴うため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当しフルリスク評価が必要と判断した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Isiro: Decline in risk during the funerals of epidemic victims - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola in Isiro, Haut-Uélé, Northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, shows a decline in risk during funerals of Ebola victims. In Isiro, Red Cross official Coco Abome said interventions are proceeding calmly and there are no remaining threats. Authorities, community leaders, and Governor Jean Bakomito are praised for ongoing sensitization and the implementation of dignified, safe burials to curb transmission. The response teams remain fully deployed, focusing on risk communication, community engagement, and base surveillance to guide elimination efforts. The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies supported the operation with equipment for the Wamba health zone, including a motorized tricycle for transporting bodies and two motorcycles for volunteer responders, enabling continued protection and routine activities. The message to communities emphasizes adherence to preventive measures to eradicate Ebola in the province.

triage.headline_ja: イシロのエボラ:流行犠牲者の葬儀における危険性の低下 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イシロでのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク対応に関する続報であり、重篤な疾患であること、国際機関(IFRC)による支援が継続していることからWPRO基準に複数該当し、フルRRAでの経過確認が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Health alert: An insecticide-resistant malaria vector is spreading rapidly.
article.articleSummary: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria mosquito that thrives in urban environments and can reproduce without rainfall, is spreading across Africa with strong insecticide resistance, threatening megacities like Lagos, Nigeria, and Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, each about 20 million residents. A Science-published study summarized by The New York Times analyzed genomes from specimens in ten countries and found resistance to all chemicals used in current vector-control campaigns. Originating in South Asia (coast of Pakistan and northern India), the species was first detected in the Horn of Africa in 2012 (Djibouti) and spread via three routes: East to Ethiopia and Kenya; across the Red Sea to Yemen; and through the Sahel to West Africa (Ghana) and southward. Public health experts warn urban populations lack immunity, and once established in cities, malaria transmission could become year-round. There are concerns it may have reached Chad, Somalia, Eritrea, and South Sudan.

triage.headline_ja: 衛生警報：殺虫剤耐性を持つマラリア媒介蚊が急速に拡大
triage.triage_reason: 都市環境に適応し全殺虫剤に耐性を持つマラリア媒介蚊（Anopheles stephensi）がアフリカの大都市に拡大しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスクの複数のIHR基準に該当するため。

article.articleHeadline: Far From A Hospital, Even A Deadly Outbreak May Go Undetected
article.articleSummary: Nature study (Gibb et al.) analyzed 58,319 infection records for 32 diseases across 169 countries and found the geography of reported outbreaks largely reflects healthcare access and detection rather than forest loss or climate. About a quarter to over a third of those at risk live more than two hours from care. Ebola spillovers in Congo illustrate under-detection; previous estimates of undetected spillovers were high, suggesting a ubiquitous, ongoing nature of spillover. article.articleHeadline: One-Pot CRISPR Test Spots Deadly Mpox Clade in 40 Minutes
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) clade I outbreaks, including the 2024 Ib sublineage and widespread 2025 cases worldwide (52,845 confirmed, 215 deaths), underscore the need for rapid, field-ready diagnostics. Researchers report a one-pot diagnostic that combines recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with CRISPR/Cas12a, delivering a fluorescent signal readable by smartphone in about 40 minutes without thermal cyclers. The assay discriminates clade I by using crRNA-I-2 and clade I–targeted primers; it uses a compartmentalized tube sleeve to keep RPA and CRISPR reagents separate during the 20-minute amplification at 39°C and then release the CRISPR mix into the reaction for a 20-minute readout at 37°C. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, pediatric cases dominate, with ~70% of confirmed cases in under-15s and ~88% of fatalities, highlighting higher virulence and the need for rapid genomic surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: ワンポットCRISPR検査、40分で危険なMpoxクレードを検出
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はMpox clade I検出のための新規診断技術（RPA+CRISPR/Cas12a）の紹介が主題であり、新たな発生や流行拡大を報じるものではない。DRCの状況は既知の背景データとして引用されているのみ。
triage.notes: 記事は診断技術（CRISPR/Cas12a併用の迅速検査法）に関する学術・技術系ニュースであり、DRCにおける小児例の割合等の統計は既存のMpox Clade I流行状況を説明する背景情報として引用されている。新規の公衆衛生イベントの発生報告ではないためDISMISSと判定。ただしMpox Clade I自体は既にPHEICとして国際的に監視されている疾病であることに留意。

article.articleHeadline: Spread of infectious diseases: Merchants should cooperate with the government to improve public health — Vikramaraja's appeal.
article.articleSummary: As Tamil Nadu's monsoon season begins, dengue fever, typhoid, and yellow fever–like mosquito- and water-borne diseases are spreading rapidly, according to a statement by A. M. Vikramaraja, president of the Confederation of Tamil Nadu Traders’ Associations. He urges merchants to display awareness posters in shops to educate customers and promote public health. The appeal underscores the need for active cooperation with the government to curb transmission and protect shoppers during the wet season. The emphasis is on awareness, early recognition of symptoms, and prompt reporting, though no case counts are provided. The call to action focuses on routine public health messaging in commerce venues across Tamil Nadu to mitigate vector- and waterborne disease risks during the monsoon.

article.articleHeadline: Rat-bite incident: HC orders joint inspection of Trichy GH
article.articleSummary: Rat-bite incident at Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital (MGMGH), Trichy, prompts the Madras High Court to order a joint inspection by the hospital dean and the Trichy Corporation Commissioner. The division bench also directs the district collector to coordinate the inspection and assess compensation feasibility for 68-year-old R Tamilkodi; case adjourned to October 15. Tamilkodi, diabetic, was bitten on the left toe by a rat on July 21 while recovering in a general ward after surgery for a leg fracture the day before. Her family had alerted authorities about rat infestation three days earlier. An advocate team found sanitation lapses: poorly maintained toilets (broken/missing doors), inadequate cleaning and water facilities, sewage leakage, stagnant drainage water, open drains near wards, rodent access, and roaming stray dogs. Counsel warns stagnant water could breed vectors such as mosquitoes, heightening risks of dengue, malaria, and secondary bacterial infections.

article.articleHeadline: Bhopal Food Safety Action: Be careful before eating! A 30-rupee tandoori being prepared among rats and cockroaches, a 600-rupee vegetable dish | Risk Of Food Poisoning From Food At Bhopal Luxury Hotels Has Increased.
article.articleSummary: Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, India — A food-safety report on 3- and 5-star hotels in Bhopal reveals hazardous kitchen conditions. For a 30-rupee tandoori and a 600-rupee vegetable dish, kitchens reportedly house rats and cockroaches on shelves, cutting areas, and cooking zones; staff health certificates and hygiene training are often missing. Mushrooms show fungal growth; onions are spoiled and potatoes rotten; samples are being tested for adulterated paneer. Ranjit Resort on Narmadapuram Road reportedly lacks staff fitness checks. Hotels such as Bhavisha Hotel & Club, Indian Café House MP Nagar, Sayaji, Tortokize, Palash, and Ranjit Lake View were cited; about 80% of large hotels had frying pans that burn black, with 12 notices issued. Gurukrupa Caterers of Bavariya reported cockroaches in the kitchen. Mycotoxins and aflatoxins from moldy produce can cause vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and liver damage; cockroaches can spread typhoid and chronic GI infections. Authorities vow action to restore food quality.

article.articleHeadline: Leptospirosis knocks in Garhwa, Jharkhand! Two cases confirmed, this is how the infection spreads during the monsoon; Health Department alert.
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis outbreaks in Garhwa district, Jharkhand, with two confirmed cases (Bardag and Kharoondi area) during the monsoon season. The infection is caused by Leptospira bacteria in water/soil contaminated with urine from animals (rats, dogs, goats, cows, buffaloes, horses). Symptoms include high fever, chills, severe headache, back and calf pain, conjunctival redness, jaundice-like appearance, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea; diagnosis is essential due to symptom overlap with dengue, malaria, or typhus. Transmission rises in rain-fed environments with standing water and mud exposure; protective measures include knee-high boots, waterproof bandages for wounds, avoiding contact with contaminated water, and using gloves, masks, and eye protection when handling animals. Testing and treatment are free at local health centers. In Bardag, four other patients have Scrub Typhus; seven total cases discussed. One additional Bardag patient tested in Latehar; results pending, samples sent to RIMS Ranchi.

triage.headline_ja: ジャールカンド州ガルワでレプトスピラ症が発生！2例確認、モンスーン期の感染拡大の仕組みとは；保健局が警戒
triage.triage_reason: インド・ジャールカンド州ガルワ地区での局地的なレプトスピラ症・ツツガムシ病の小規模発生であり、重症度・国際的拡大リスクは低いが、モンスーン期の環境曝露継続や動物由来感染経路があるため経過観察が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Fake Drug Racket Busted In Delhi; 481 Units Of Counterfeit Rabies Vaccine Seized
article.articleSummary: Delhi's Drugs Control Department busted a major fake drug racket in Bhagirath Palace, seizing 481 counterfeit units of Human IP Rabies Vaccine (Purified Vero Cell Rabies Vaccine, Abhayrab) worth about Rs 2 lakh. After a tip‑off, raids on three premises confirmed the batch was not issued by the original manufacturer, M/S Human Biological Institute, Telangana; samples have been sent to the CRI Centre in Kasauli for quality testing. 120 vials were retained as samples; 361 were seized along with seven purchase invoices under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 (Sections 22(1)(C) and 22(1)(CC)). The network traces to an agency in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh; UP authorities raided two Kanpur locations and the agency admitted supplying Delhi. Delhi and UP are jointly investigating to identify the kingpin and distribution chain. Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh pledged zero tolerance and strict action.

article.articleHeadline: Barabanki News: Communicable disease control campaign confined to paperwork; infections in villages have increased due to unsanitary conditions.
article.articleSummary: Barabanki district reports rising dengue and malaria infections amid deteriorating sanitation, with four deaths and a growing fever caseload. Officials say vector-control campaigns remain largely on paper as regular cleaning and anti-larvae spraying falter, while garbage piles and water stagnation from city to village fuel mosquito breeding. In Suratganj town, despite waste-disposal claims, dumps near the fish market and the BRC office emit odors and hinder movement; similar debris problems persist elsewhere. In Masouli block’s 56 Gram Panchayats, blocked drains and heaps of grass, straw, and litter leave standing water after rain, heightening mosquito risk. The Barabanki CHC at Badgaon is seeing crowded fever clinics, with many patients visiting informal practitioners. Reported are suspected dengue, malaria, and fever cases, underscoring that unsanitary conditions are driving ongoing transmission rather than effective outbreak control.

triage.headline_ja: バラバンキ発:感染症対策キャンペーンは書類上のみ、不衛生な環境により村での感染が増加
triage.triage_reason: インド・バラバンキ地区でデング熱・マラリアが季節性に増加し死者も出ているが、これは例年見られる地方規模の媒介蚊由来感染症であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。衛生対策の不備により感染が継続する可能性があるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 地方紙（ヒンディー語）の報道で、バラバンキ地区における衛生管理不備によるデング熱・マラリアの季節性流行を伝える内容。死亡者4名の報告があるが、地域レベルの公衆衛生問題であり国際的な懸念には至っていない。

article.articleHeadline: In view of fever spreading in Sahjan, the CMO conducted an inspection and met the families of the deceased.
article.articleSummary: In Sahjan village, Mohammadi block, Lakhimpur Kheri district, Uttar Pradesh, fever cases and two deaths triggered a health alert on 23 Sept 2026. Chief Medical Officer Dr. Santosh Gupta, village officials, and health teams conducted a ground inspection. Archana, 23, died 28 Aug 2026; preliminary cause: typhoid and infection. Pratibha, 17, developed fever on 13 Sept 2026 and died en route to Shahjahanpur after 13–14 Sept deterioration; preliminary diagnosis: acute abdomen. Sanitation issues identified: drinking water lines passing through drains, a dirty pond nearby, and a pig enclosure outside the village, potentially fostering infections. Immediate actions: cleaning and sanitation, fogging for vector control, and door-to-door surveys with vaccination; CHC supervisor to collect samples for malaria, dengue, typhoid, and Japanese encephalitis. Residents told to boil water or use government handpump water. A health camp treated 156, with 130 tested (1 malaria, 1 typhoid); chlorine tablets distributed; a follow-up camp planned for Thursday.

triage.headline_ja: サハジャン村で発熱が拡大する中、CMOが視察を実施し、死亡者の家族と面会

article.articleHeadline: Suspected food poisoning: Health officials inspect beverage outlet in Kannur
article.articleSummary: Suspected food poisoning linked to a popular beverage outlet at Caltex in Kannur. On September 21, seven members of a Kannur family who drank cocktails from the outlet developed health problems and sought treatment at Kolachery Primary Health Centre. Health and Food Safety officials inspected the outlet on September 23 after the complaints. Several others, including children, reportedly sought medical care and are under observation. Samples from the outlet will be sent for laboratory testing to identify the cause. The cases were reported to the Health department, and authorities are monitoring the situation as investigations continue; no laboratory-confirmed diagnosis is reported in the article. Updates will follow pending test results to determine infection source and any need for public health action.

article.articleHeadline: Supaul News: Supaul: Rural Doctors Receive Training in the Prevention of Infectious Diseases.
article.articleSummary: On 23 September 2026, Ragho Pur Referral Hospital in Supaul organized a one-day training for rural doctors on identifying, preventing, and promptly reporting infectious diseases. Dozens of rural physicians from across Supaul district attended. The program aimed to equip participants to recognize early symptoms at the local level and relay information to the health department quickly to curb disease spread. Trainer Sumir Kumar Singh outlined identifying early signs, reporting suspected cases, and urgently referring severe patients to the nearest government hospital; BVDS Sanjit Kumar Singh noted that timely detection and reporting substantially aid containment. Emphasized warning signs such as fever, cough, breathing difficulty, skin rashes, and specifically kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) and filariasis. Emphasis on personal hygiene, safe drinking water, handwashing, and community education, including awareness about both infectious and non-communicable diseases. Officials and many rural doctors attended, urged to implement measures locally and report suspected cases without delay.

article.articleHeadline: Chhattisgarh: 11-km trek takes health team to remote Dantewada village, four critical cases detected
article.articleSummary: An 11-km trek through Bailadila hills to Lohagaon, a remote village in Kuakonda block, Chhattisgarh's Bastar district, screened 62 residents, detecting four urgent cases: a pregnant woman, a cataract patient, and two malaria-positive individuals. The health camp also screened for malaria and sickle cell disease, and flagged suspected cataract and leprosy cases. Antenatal check-ups and children’s vaccinations were provided. This was the village’s first comprehensive health screening camp, reducing the need to travel to facilities. Conducted under the Mukhyamantri Swasth Bastar campaign, the district has 76 health points to extend services to remote settlements. The visit highlights persistent access barriers in Bastar’s interior, where service delivery depends on physical reach, not just facility availability, and emphasizes the need for timely referrals for high-risk patients.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue is frightening! No fever, yet weakness persists? Why is the 4-6 day period the most dangerous time for dengue? What doctors are saying.
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Kolkata, India, is rising amid monsoon heat with DENV-1 to DENV-4 circulating; DENV-2 and DENV-4 are linked to more severe disease, and some patients show co-infections with multiple serotypes. ICMR reports all four serotypes spreading in some states. The illness can involve multiple organs, including hepatitis, myocarditis, and nervous system effects, necessitating regular monitoring. A critical phase typically occurs around days 4–6 after fever onset, during which hemoconcentration may occur and the immune response intensifies; IgM and IgG antibodies become detectable as fever subsides. Platelet counts begin to drop around day 4, with transfusion required if they fall below 10,000/μL. Management is primarily supportive: fever control, dehydration prevention, adequate fluid intake, urine output monitoring, and serial labs of hematopoietic parameters and liver function. Remarks by Dr. Dipankar Sarkar, Senior Consultant Internal Medicine and Critical Care, Manipal Hospital, Salt Lake, underscore the need for continuous observation.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱は恐ろしい！熱は下がったのに、なぜだるさが続くのか？発症4〜6日目がデング熱で最も危険な理由とは。医師が解説。
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はコルカタにおけるデング熱の臨床経過・重症化サインについての医師による一般向け医療解説記事であり、新規の異常な発生や急激な増加を報告するものではない。デング熱はインドで季節性・地域流行的に発生する既知の疾患であり、シグナルとしての特異性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Two dengue-positive cases, including a doctor, at SKMCH; risk increased due to lack of fogging on the premises - skmch dengue cases fogging crisis
article.articleSummary: Two dengue-positive cases confirmed at Shri Krishna Medical College and Hospital (SKMCH) in Muzaffarpur after antigen testing, including a doctor and a female patient, triggering fear among clinicians, students, and nursing staff. The hospital campus is plagued by garbage, waterlogging, and overgrown vegetation that boost mosquito breeding. Despite the presence of fogging machines for two years, no fogging has been carried out on the premises, signaling administrative neglect. District health authorities report 31 dengue cases in Muzaffarpur, with Mushahari block accounting for 16 cases; Bochahan and Kanti each report 2; Meenapur 3; Motipur 1; others scattered. Dengue wards have been established at SKMCH and Sadar Hospital, with mosquito nets on every bed and ongoing patient monitoring. Urgent calls for comprehensive fogging, larvicidal spraying, and vegetation clearance aim to curb further spread.

article.articleHeadline: FMD outbreak: Arunachal minister orders deployment of 2 additional teams in Dibang Valley
article.articleSummary: Arunachal Pradesh's Dibang Valley faces an ongoing foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak, prompting on Wednesday the deployment of two additional expert rapid response teams to the district. The new teams join one already operating in the affected area and will be equipped with medicines, disinfectants, diagnostic support, logistics and mobility facilities. They will assist district authorities with disease investigation, sample collection and containment, while intensifying village-level surveillance and awareness campaigns for early detection of suspected cases. Farmers and livestock owners will be briefed on early reporting, movement restrictions, and biosecurity practices to curb spread. The minister also ordered ring vaccination in identified areas to create a protective buffer around affected locations and instructed daily monitoring by the secretary of the animal husbandry department.

article.articleHeadline: Hepatitis A attack on children with a viral infection.
article.articleSummary: Bagpat district, Uttar Pradesh, India, reports a surge in pediatric viral infections accompanied by Hepatitis A. In the last three months, both private and government hospitals have recorded record caseloads. Of 100 admitted cases, 60 involve Viral Hepatitis A. Symptoms include fever lasting 3–4 days, followed by jaundice, abdominal pain, vomiting, and loss of appetite; fever often precedes jaundice. Liver enzymes SGPT and SGOT are markedly elevated, complicating recovery. Oxygen levels are falling, with pneumonia-like respiratory distress reported; nebulizers are used to stabilize patients. Recovery for hepatic illness and associated respiratory symptoms typically spans 10–15 days. Pediatricians note that standard viral symptoms—sore throat and cough—remain common, but concurrent Hepatitis A infection prolongs illness duration. The article does not report fatalities.

triage.headline_ja: ウッタル・プラデーシュ州で小児にウイルス感染とともにA型肝炎が流行

article.articleHeadline: Dengue Awareness Camp
article.articleSummary: Dengue Awareness Camp conducted at the school, with principal Ma. Th. Ajay Kumar inaugurating the event and distributing Nilavembu Kudineer to students. Coordinator Vasanth Raj led proceedings, and Chief Minister Sathyia Sabareesan welcomed attendees. article.articleHeadline: 7 Things to Do During the First Rain After the Dry Season, Prevent Dengue Fever and Leaky Roofs
article.articleSummary: First rain after the dry season in Indonesia heightens dengue fever risk as Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed in standing water. Practical guidance emphasizes home and road safety. Before heavy rains, clean gutters, drains, and roofs to prevent overflow. Inspect roofs, flashing, and joints for leaks and seal or replace damaged sections. Roads become unusually slick due to residual oil and dust; motorists should slow down, use headlights, maintain safe distances, and ensure tires and brakes are in good condition. After the rain, wash vehicles promptly to remove dust and pollutants that can dull paint and corrode metal; check undercarriages, brakes, and electricals, especially for motorcycles. During the seasonal transition, authorities warn that standing water fosters dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti, raising dengue fever risk in Indonesia.

article.articleHeadline: High Influenza Transmission During the Dry Season, Here’s the Explanation.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, Indonesian experts note that influenza transmission remains high during the dry season, despite drier air generally reducing virus survival. Crowding in indoor spaces and limited sunlight inflate transmission risk. In urban settings with air pollution, closed rooms without adequate ventilation further sustain spread. Daycare centers are particularly vulnerable, where several children sharing a room can rapidly propagate infection and cleaning of contaminated surfaces may be insufficient. A single influenza case can, on average, infect about three others, with the exact rate influenced by environmental conditions, weather, and how densely people gather indoors. The explanation emphasizes indoor transmission dynamics and the role of ventilation and sun exposure in mitigating spread during Indonesia’s dry season.

article.articleHeadline: Respiratory Syncytial Virus to Enter the Epidemic Season; the elderly and the very young are high-risk groups; antibiotic treatment is ineffective.
article.articleSummary: RSV enters its typical peak season (October–April). Beijing You’an Hospital infectious disease expert Li Tongzeng notes there is no specific antiviral; treatment is supportive. Young children, especially under one year, and older adults with COPD, diabetes, or immune compromise are high-risk for pneumonia and potentially respiratory failure. Early RSV symptoms resemble a common cold—nasal congestion, runny nose, mild cough and fever—but RSV can progress to lower respiratory tract infection with higher fever, wheeze, chest tightness, and, in infants, irritability or poor feeding. Most mild cases can be managed at home with rest, fluids, antipyretics, saline nasal irrigation, and humidification; nebulization may relieve symptoms. Severe cases require hospitalization with oxygen and respiratory support. A long-acting monoclonal antibody is approved in China for infants under six months or those with congenital heart disease or chronic lung disease to reduce infection and severe outcomes. Adults have low risk but can transmit to high-risk household members; emphasize ventilation, hand hygiene, and masking in enclosed spaces.

article.articleHeadline: Bacillary Dysentery, a Bacterial Disease, Can Cause Bloody Diarrhea; Learn the Symptoms from Cleveland Clinic | Bacillary Dysentery Bloody Diarrhea Symptoms
article.articleSummary: Bacillary dysentery, commonly called Shigellosis, is a bacterial infection of the large intestine caused by Shigella, causing inflammation and ulcers that yield bloody, mucus-laden stools, cramps, fever, and dehydration. Cleveland Clinic notes it spreads rapidly, person-to-person, via poor sanitation, contaminated water or food, and unwashed hands; symptoms typically appear 1–3 days after exposure. Key signs include bloody diarrhea, severe abdominal cramps, fever, tenesmus, nausea, vomiting, and weakness. Diagnosis relies on stool testing to identify Shigella and guide antibiotics; antibiotics are often needed in severe cases. Do not use anti-diarrheal medicines, which can worsen infection. Management emphasizes rehydration with ORS, coconut water, and clear fluids, plus light foods (khichdi, porridge, banana, yogurt). Prevention focuses on handwashing, safe water, cooked foods, and washing produce. Seek care if blood in stool, fever above 101°F, or persistent dehydration. article.articleHeadline: A Single Histone Tag Decides Whether Malaria Parasites Commit to
article.articleSummary: Malaria parasite Plasmodium yoelii uses a ubiquitin-dependent epigenetic switch to decide sexual commitment (gametocytogenesis), essential for transmission to mosquitoes. In a Nature Microbiology study by Zhiwei Jiao, Lirong Lin, Ruoyu Tang and colleagues from Xiamen University and Tongji University (China), deletion of E2 enzyme Rad6B disrupted gametocyte production and severely impaired oocyst formation in the mosquito midgut, with parasite levels in mice similar to wild-type, indicating a transmission-specific defect. Rad6B partners with RING-type E3 ligase Tex1; both require catalytic activity. The Rad6B-Tex1 complex monoubiquitinates histone H2B, enabling H3K4me3 at the ap2-g promoter and triggering ap2-g expression; loss of this modification suppresses sexual commitment. ChIP-seq and CUT&Tag-seq show reduced H2B monoubiquitination at target loci in mutants. The mechanism is conserved in Plasmodium falciparum, linking a single histone modification to malaria transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Child with high fever and sore throat, refusing to eat: beware of herpangina.
article.articleSummary: Herpangina is an acute enterovirus infection primarily affecting children under six, per Fujian Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Transmission occurs via fecal-oral, respiratory droplets, and direct contact, with outbreaks common in nurseries and kindergartens. Sudden fever (39–41°C) peaks within 24–48 hours, followed by sore throat and pharyngeal redness with scattered gray-white vesicles (1–2 mm) around a red halo; these vesicles rupture to yellow ulcers within 2–3 days. Young children may refuse meals, drool, and be irritable; swallowing is painful. There is no specific antiviral treatment; management is supportive: antipyretics, cooling, fluids, and soft, cool foods, plus mouth care. The illness is usually self-limiting within about a week; rare cases progress to persistent fever, rapid breathing, somnolence, or tremors requiring medical care. Prevention emphasizes handwashing, reduced gatherings, disinfection, and morning screening in childcare settings.

article.articleHeadline: Brazilian Agroforests Harbor Surprising Mosquito Diversity and Disease
article.articleSummary: Three-year study (2022–2025) at Terra Boa Farm, Silva Jardim, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil documented 5,314 immature mosquitoes from 38 species. Culex dominated (53.8%), followed by Limatus (16.6%) and Wyeomyia (16.2%); five species—Cx. iridescens, Cx. pleuristriatus, Lim. durhamii, Wy. edwardsi, and Ae. albopictus—made up about 80% of captures. Natural habitats (bromeliads, bamboo internodes, peach palm bracts) yielded 4,175 specimens (78.6%) and 34 species, with 26 exclusive to natural sites; bromeliads produced 2,031 individuals from 22 species. Bamboo internodes were dominated by Cx. iridescens (72.4%) and harbored Toxorhynchites trichopygus larvae. Artificial containers (tarps and a 200-L barrel) held 1,139 specimens from 12 species, led by Li. durhamii and Ae. albopictus (tarps 83.7%). Cx. quinquefasciatus appeared in tarps; sylvatic yellow fever vectors Haemagogus leucocelaenus/janthinomys and Sabethes identicus were found in bamboo near Poço das Antas reserve, signaling spillover risk and the ecological plasticity of vectors in agroforestry, with Ae. albopictus as a generalist.

article.articleHeadline: The contagious disease that hit Ronaldinho and his entourage, what is 'Yellow Fever'?
article.articleSummary: Ronaldinho and members of his entourage were detained at Kochi airport for not presenting Yellow Fever vaccination certificates before entering India for the Return of the Titans series; entry was allowed after presenting a digital certificate. Yellow Fever is a mosquito-borne viral disease, found mainly in Africa and tropical Americas; most infections are mild, but severe disease can cause liver and kidney failure and bleeding, with a case-fatality rate of 30-60% in severe cases. There is no specific antiviral treatment, but a single-dose vaccine provides long-lasting protection; international certificates become valid 10 days after vaccination. At-risk regions include Angola, Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Cameroon, DR Congo, and in the Americas Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, and Venezuela. Kerala faces heightened risk due to high Aedes aegypti density; past Zika virus was reported in Thiruvananthapuram in 2022. Emphasized are travel health checks, vector control, disease surveillance, and public awareness to prevent cross-border spread.

article.articleHeadline: Connectivity between hatcheries increases disease risk in aquaculture.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian researchers at Embrapa Pesca e Aquicultura, in partnership with Italy's IZSVe, applied an Italian GIS-based methodology to map areas vulnerable to waterborne disease spread among aquaculture operations. They show that connectivity among hatcheries within the same watershed increases disease dissemination risk, prompting development of high/medium/low contamination maps to guide rapid response in emergencies. The protocol, originally developed for animal health surveillance and calamities such as avian influenza, was adapted to study the acantocéfalo (acanthocephalan) parasite affecting tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum). The parasite's eggs in fish feces reach ostracods (intermediate hosts); healthy fish become infected by feeding on contaminated ostracods, with the full cycle lasting about two months. Infected fish may lose up to 20% of potential weight, imposing economic costs. The study, triggered by a 2015 Rondônia outbreak, suggests GIS-informed risk zoning can strengthen surveillance and be applied to other species.

article.articleHeadline: Latin America on alert over the arrival of El Niño, threatening floods, pollution and diseases.
article.articleSummary: El Niño is active and Latin America faces potential floods, water contamination, and dengue risk as temperatures rise and rainfall intensifies. An OPS 2026-2027 assessment warns of health risks under both wet and dry scenarios across the region, with parts of Ecuador, Peru, Colombia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina identified as areas where floods, displacement, and water- or vector-borne diseases may increase. Higher temperatures can accelerate Aedes mosquito development and shorten the virus incubation period, potentially elevating dengue transmission when conditions are favorable. Drought conditions may lead households to store water, creating mosquito breeding sites. After floods or droughts, weakened water and sanitation systems can worsen disease spread. A 2026 international study found a link between El Niño intensity and dengue risk, though outcomes vary by locale. Importantly, El Niño arrival does not automatically raise cases; local surveillance and prevention matter.

article.articleHeadline: Climate change requires municipal contingency plans and heightened vigilance against rising arboviral diseases.
article.articleSummary: Brazil faces rising arboviral threats as extreme climate and the Super El Niño push dengue projections to 1.7 million in coming months, according to Fiocruz-based government estimates. Dengue, Zika, and chikungunya transmitted by Aedes aegypti are of concern; the Ministry of Health warns of increasing arboviruses. Peak transmission historically December–April/May, but climate anomalies could raise cases outside the typical season, though large-scale epidemics this period are unlikely. Early diagnosis and rapid testing are crucial for correct treatment, vector control, and case notification to slow transmission. Pregnant women require heightened vigilance due to Zika’s risk of fetal malformations. Contingency planning is urged for public and private sectors, including reorganizing services for rapid care, hydration hubs to reduce dengue complications, and healthcare worker training to differentiate arbovirus symptoms. Vaccination remains key for primary prevention; elimination of standing water continues as essential.

article.articleHeadline: Brazil will have a reserve to produce 10 million doses of foot-and-mouth disease vaccine.
article.articleSummary: Brazil will maintain a reserve of frozen foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) vaccine antigens capable of producing up to 10 million doses in an emergency. The stock is stored at Biogénesis Bagó’s laboratory in Garín, Greater Buenos Aires, through a partnership with Brazil’s MAPA, the Paraná Institute of Technology (Tecpar), and Biogénesis Bagó. Antigens, not ready vaccines, enable rapid vaccine formulation while reducing expiry risk. If an outbreak occurs, the antigen can be thawed and vaccine formulated within four days, with doses reaching the affected region within seven days, contingent on production readiness. Brazil suspended FMD vaccination in May 2024; in May 2025, the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE) recognized the country as FMD-free without vaccination. Surveillance continues, and producers must maintain biosafety and report suspicions. Vaccination would be reintroduced only after virus identification and official assessment by MAPA and Panaftosa. The reserve is part of broader emergency preparedness to protect exports while maintaining FMD-free status.

Transmission is driven by sexual spread, shared injection equipment, and limited treatment access, exacerbated by stigma. A new diagnosis does not always reflect a recent infection, and expanded testing may contribute to rising counts. Brazil reported 39,216 HIV cases in 2024, underscoring prevention measures (PrEP, PEP, condoms, testing). With treatment, people can reach undetectable viral loads and prevent sexual transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Seafood contaminated with poisonous crabs could trigger a major disaster; during crab season, beware these marine "toxins"
article.articleSummary: Published 2026-09-23. Seafood contaminated with poisonous crabs could trigger a major disaster during crab season. A market incident where a small crab mixed with squid was identified as a red-spotted crab carrying tetrodotoxin; even tiny amounts can be fatal, and high-heat cooking does not destroy the toxin. The article lists dangerous marine organisms and regions: red-spotted crab and copper-crusted crab (both with tetrodotoxin) found around Japan, the Philippines, Singapore, and China’s Guangdong and Hainan; textile cone snail and blue-ringed octopus with tetrodotoxin; box jellyfish with severe venom. Spoiled shrimp and crabs can harbor Vibrio parahaemolyticus, reaching pathogenic levels within six hours at 35°C. Prevention tips: avoid unfamiliar seafood, buy from reputable markets, keep raw and cooked seafood separate, and cook to 100°C. Vulnerable groups should avoid raw or undercooked seafood. Three rules: don’t eat unfamiliar, don’t buy unfamiliar, don’t handle unfamiliar seafood.

article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, Aurora province in Central Luzon, Philippines reports dengue cases rising 137% to 2,172. Baler added 11 new infections (total 242); Casiguran 8 (total 253). Dipaculao and Dinalungan each reported 1 new case (totals 69 and 37). Dilasag has the highest attack rate at 23.2 per 1,000. Dengue clusters span 61 barangays; transmission is not confined to a single municipality. Nationwide, 155,918 cases (−33% YoY), Central Luzon highest region with 21,242. Health measures urge elimination of breeding sites, nets, repellents, prompt medical consultation, and targeted fogging where needed; early detection remains critical as rains continue.

article.articleHeadline: Cebu City culls 57 hogs infected with ASF virus

Blood testing and surveillance continue; authorities are tracing possible sources from outside Cebu City, with potential links to Consolacion, Liloan, and Lapu-Lapu City; no supplier identified yet. Some raisers resist blood sampling, fearing immediate culling and loss of aid. Indemnification offers fixed amounts (P4,000 for pigs 21–90 days, P8,000 for hogs 25–70 kg, P12,000 for sows) with registration; unregistered raisers may access social welfare support. Depopulation remains possible near confirmed areas.

article.articleHeadline: Shrimp-Killing Vibrio Genomes Reveal Toxin and Secretion Weaponry Are Not
article.articleSummary: Acute Hepatopancreatic Necrosis Disease (AHPND) in shrimp, blamed for wiping out farms across Asia and the Americas, is not as genetically simple as once thought. A BMC Genomics study by Contante and colleagues shows the type VI secretion system (T6SS) is not a reliable driver of AHPND. The team sequenced four Philippine isolates—Vibrio parahaemolyticus PH1339 and PH1273, and Vibrio campbellii PH1401 and PH1409—and analyzed 807 public genomes. They found three T6SS clusters (T6SS1–T6SS3). T6SS1 appears in both AHPND-causing and non-AHPND strains; T6SS2 is present in all four; T6SS3 is limited to V. campbellii. Although pirAB toxin genes on a ~70 kb plasmid co-occurred with T6SS1/2 at first glance, a phylogeny-aware analysis showed no significant link after accounting for shared ancestry. Thus, T6SS is not a reliable diagnostic marker for AHPND; surveillance should focus on the pirAB toxin rather than T6SS presence.

article.articleHeadline: At the start of the new school year, parents should do this to protect their child from Japanese encephalitis.
article.articleSummary: Japanese encephalitis, a mosquito-borne viral disease, is particularly a concern in Vietnam as the school year begins and rainy, warm weather create more Culex mosquito activity. Initial symptoms include fever, headache, nausea; severe cases may lead to lethargy, seizures, and altered consciousness, with risk of long-term neurological or cognitive impairment. WHO notes there is no specific antiviral treatment; care is supportive, and fatality among symptomatic cases can reach about 30%, with 20–30% of survivors incurring lasting sequelae. Vietnam’s Expanded Program on Immunization uses three primary JEV doses: at age 1 year (dose 1), 1–2 weeks later (dose 2), and one year after dose 1 (dose 3). Booster doses are recommended every 3 years until age 15. Parents should check vaccination records, ensure boosters are up to date, and combine immunization with mosquito control measures (bed nets, long clothing, removing standing water). If records are missing, consult a vaccination center for a tailored schedule.

article.articleHeadline: Strengthening the prevention and control of infectious diseases for children.
article.articleSummary: As schools reopen, families and educators intensify preventive measures against infectious diseases, notably hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD). In Cam Đường, Bình Minh campus, pre-schoolers are taught daily hygiene, with classrooms cleaned, surfaces sanitized, and good ventilation prioritized. Parents screen children for fever or mouth ulcers before attendance and model handwashing with soap, avoiding mouth contact with objects. HFMD, caused by an enterovirus, presents with fever and sore throat; 1–2 days later, painful mouth ulcers and vesicles on hands, feet, and in the mouth may appear; some cases have oral lesions only. Dr. Dang Thi Quynh of Lao Cai Regional Health Center–Cam Đường notes the importance of “3 sạch” — eating clean, living clean, and hands clean — to limit transmission. The province issued guidance to boost surveillance for polio, HFMD, dengue, influenza, measles, and meningococcal meningitis; education and health sectors mandate clean environments and early reporting, with vaccination catch-up where needed.

article.articleHeadline: Measles is making a comeback- Will we end it for good?
article.articleSummary: Measles is resurging in the Western Pacific after decades of progress toward elimination. The region, home to 2.2 billion people, saw a rebound linked to COVID-19 vaccination challenges and antivaccine misinformation. WHO notes that elimination by 2030 is possible, building on the record that measles vaccination has saved 94 million lives globally, including 12 million in Western Pacific, with vaccination preventing 154 million deaths since 1974. In 2025, Western Pacific recorded over 1.6 million zero-dose children—most at risk. Last year, WHO certified measles and rubella eliminated as public health threats in all 21 Pacific island countries and areas. Nine countries remain to reach elimination: Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Mongolia, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Vietnam; they must maintain strong routine immunization, surveillance, and rapid outbreak response, not rely on campaigns alone. Investment is essential; measles is a sentinel for health system strength. Dr Saia Ma'u Piukala.

article.articleHeadline: Controlling the Risk of Dengue Fever.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Thanh Hóa Province, Vietnam, as of 13 September 2026, totals 104 cases or suspected cases, down 32 from the same period in 2025. Week 37 (7–13 Sept) recorded 4 cases, down 6 from the previous week; no deaths and no community outbreak, with case numbers remaining low for several weeks. Authorities emphasize proactive, ground-level prevention: risk surveillance, community guidance on eliminating mosquito breeding sites, and early intervention. Hà Trung District’s Health Center directs health stations to spray disinfectants and clean environments. In 9 months of 2026, communes under Hà Trung reported no dengue cases, yet preventive measures persist; in Hà Tiến, June surveillance flagged two high larval indices, prompting chemical spraying, environmental sanitation, and larval control in two villages with ongoing monitoring. Public education urges covering water containers, removing stagnant water, releasing fish, and reporting risk factors. Northern regions report 240 dengue cases, down 55% weekly, year-to-date 5,225 cases, up 64% YoY; Thanh Hóa remains lower, underscoring the need for sustained surveillance and community action. Dr. Đỗ Thái Hòa highlights continued cross-sector risk management and household vigilance.

article.articleHeadline: Weasel Bite Linked to Deadly Tick-Borne Virus in Rare Chinese Case
article.articleSummary: Five days after a bite from a Siberian weasel (Mustela sibirica) in Dalian, Liaoning Province, China, a 55-year-old woman developed fever, malaise and diarrhea. Laboratory tests showed thrombocytopenia and multi-organ dysfunction. On day 12 of illness, metagenomic next-generation sequencing detected SFTSV (severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus) in peripheral blood, confirming infection. SFTSV, a Bandavirus in Phenuiviridae, is traditionally tick-borne and primarily transmitted by Haemaphysalis longicornis; outbreaks have been reported in China, South Korea, Japan and Vietnam, with case-fatality rates ranging about 5-20%. While ticks are the main vector, the virus circulates in cattle, goats, dogs, cats, and wild mammals. This case documents a direct mammal-to-human transmission via a bite, implying that wild carnivores could contribute to human exposure, particularly in rural northeastern China.

article.articleHeadline: Three-year delay in surgery leaves a woman with sepsis and spinal abscess.
article.articleSummary: 62-year-old woman from Vinh Long, Vietnam, presented after a three-year delay in spine surgery due to fear, with epidural abscess compressing neural structures and bilateral psoas abscess. MRI and labs showed severe infection; culture grew Escherichia coli. She has type 2 diabetes, hypertension, osteoporosis, and chronic adrenal insufficiency. Management followed a stepwise approach: resuscitation, glycemic control, correction of systemic derangements, and culture-guided antibiotics. Once stabilized, surgeons performed decompression, abscess drainage, and posterior spinal stabilization across the lumbar–sacral region. The six-hour operation faced inflamed tissue, nerve edema, osteopenia, and significant bleeding; infected tissue was removed, nerves freed, and the spine stabilized. Postoperatively, antibiotics continued and wound healing progressed. At discharge, lower-limb strength remained 2/5, but she could sit with a brace and begin standing and ambulating with assistance. The report stresses timely surgical evaluation and warns against delaying surgery in elderly or immunocompromised patients.

article.articleHeadline: Thai Nguyen reports African swine fever outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Thai Nguyen Province, Vietnam, reported an African swine fever outbreak in Hiep Luc commune, Na Khu hamlet, Thuần Mang village. An imported herd of 41 pigs, bought online with unclear origin and lacking veterinary certification, showed illness: 15 symptomatic and 5 dead at inspection on 18 September. Local authorities isolated sick stock, culled dead animals, and carried out disinfection. By 20 September they culled 14 severely ill pigs and 6 dead; laboratory tests confirmed African swine fever. On 23 September a further 16 infected pigs were culled. Authorities warn farmers to halt movement, report abnormal pig mortality promptly, and prevent carcass disposal in the environment. The outbreak underscores ongoing risk in Thai Nguyen, where 2025 data show 4,962 households affected across 78 of 92 communes, with 35,715 pigs culled and over 1,701 tons destroyed. Smallholder farming in northern areas without full biosafety practices fuels recurrent outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: A doctor recommended that tourists from Thailand undergo a test if they have COVID-19 symptoms - News on Vesti.ru.
article.articleSummary: Tourists returning from Thailand to Russia may bring COVID-19, with spread depending on how quickly the pathogen is localized and on potential changes in the virus. Moscow-based infectious disease physician Georgiy Vikulov told NEWS.ru that travelers with COVID-19 symptoms during or after travel should not self-medicate, but urgently seek medical evaluation. Molecular diagnostics can rapidly identify the exact pathogen or pathogens, and co-infections are possible, guiding appropriate treatment. Tests can be performed outside clinics in network laboratories; rapid tests exist that can simultaneously detect COVID-19, influenza, and other respiratory agents. Vikulov noted that infection can progress with few or no symptoms in people with greater resistance. Previously, Russian tour operators did not warn travelers about COVID-19 risk in Thailand and did not cancel already paid trips.

article.articleHeadline: A warning to gardeners! A 65-year-old woman walking barefoot on soil contracted a burrowing parasite ('hookworm') that caused itching from scratching and led to a spreading infection.
article.articleSummary: 65-year-old woman in Thailand with diabetes and hypertension developed creeping eruption (cutaneous larva migrans) after walking barefoot in a soursop orchard. She presented with blistering, inflamed foot lesions that progressed to purulent discharge within a day despite antibiotics. Examination revealed serpiginous, reddish tracks consistent with skin-penetrating nematode larvae. The infection was caused by hookworm larvae from dog/cat feces—or Strongyloides—in soil. In this patient, diabetes and marked pruritus led to scratching and secondary bacterial infection (Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes) in the dermis. The condition is not life-threatening; larvae remain in the epidermis as incidental hosts and typically die over weeks. Treatment included oral anthelmintic Albendazole 400 mg daily for 3–7 days, antihistamines, and a short course of topical steroids; antibiotics such as Dicloxacillin or Cephalexin, plus topical mupirocin or fusidic acid for infected skin. Prevention: avoid barefoot exposure.

article.articleHeadline: Don't let a box of mooncakes land you a million-dollar fine! New Taipei City Animal Protection Office urges a ban on overseas meat products entering the country to prevent African swine fever.
article.articleSummary: As of Sep 24, 2026, the New Taipei City Department of Animal Protection and Epidemic Prevention urged banning overseas meat and meat products to prevent African swine fever (ASF) importation. Overseas meat products, including meat floss mooncakes and meat-filled pastries, and vacuum-packed items are prohibited. Under Taiwan's Animal Infectious Disease Prevention and Control Act, travelers violating import rules face NT$10,000–NT$1,000,000 in fines; first offenses by travelers from ASF-affected countries within the past three years carry NT$200,000, with second offenses reaching NT$1,000,000. From 2026 through Aug 23, border checks detected 143 ASF nucleic acid–positive pork products: 137 from China, 2 from Vietnam, 4 from Thailand. New Taipei City reports active biosecurity work: disinfecting 6,332 transport vehicles; 102 pig farms visited; 832 inspections; 132 serology tests. Emphasizes disruptions at source, border, and farm levels to reduce ASF risk.

article.articleHeadline: Floods, hunger and diseases worsen suffering in Myanmar amid the war.
article.articleSummary: Flooding from the monsoon since July worsens Myanmar’s war-driven humanitarian crisis. The World Health Organization reports floods affecting more than 470,000 people, with rising malaria, dengue, and cholera outbreaks. Nearly four million people are internally displaced, and access remains blocked by fighting and multiple checkpoints. In Shwebo, Sagaing Region, and central Magway, conflict disrupts aid delivery and inflates costs. The UN’s OCHA warns Myanmar is among the world’s gravest crises, with over 16 million in need and partners reaching about 1.6 million by March. Food prices have surged amid higher fuel and fertilizer costs linked to the Russia-Ukraine war and Iranian blockades of the Strait of Hormuz after US and Israel attacks. Skin infections such as scabies are common; the Ayeyarwady Delta’s crops are threatened as harvest approaches, and regime recruitment exceeds 100,000.
